problem: The left-sided case is garbled and unreadable: "If the ROC is |z| m. Read x[−m] as the coefficient of zm." The condition and the series have lost text, so a student cannot tell what the ROC test is or which series to read.
fix: If the ROC is |z| < r, the sequence is left-sided, so divide to get a series in positive powers of z: X(z) = Σ x[−m] z^m. Read x[−m] as the coefficient of z^m.

problem: The second case is garbled: "|z| k| gives −pknu[−n−1]". The inequality has lost its left side and the exponent is unreadable.
Garbled sentence about the pole at the origin: "it appears for n n−1 then has a negative power". The condition on n is missing and the reason is cut off.
fix: Include a pole at z = 0 when it lies inside C; for n < 0 the factor zⁿ⁻¹ is a negative power of z, so z = 0 becomes a pole of X(z) zⁿ⁻¹ and adds a residue.

problem: The inside/outside mapping is inverted. The contour C lies inside the ROC, so a pole with |p| < radius of C is inside the contour and gives the right-sided term aⁿu[n] (ROC |z| > |a|); a pole outside C gives the left-sided term. The answer states the opposite.
fix: X(z) alone does not fix the sequence. The ROC fixes each pole's position relative to C: a pole inside the contour (|p| smaller than the radius of C, i.e. ROC |z| > |p|) gives the right-sided term pⁿu[n]; a pole outside it (ROC |z| < |p|) gives the left-sided term −pⁿu[−n−1]. Same partial fractions, different sequence.

problem: The premise is impossible: a pole at z = 2 cannot lie inside the ROC 1 < |z| < 3, because the ROC never contains a pole. The given answer then also inverts the rule, calling a pole at |z| = 2 with |z| < 3 "outside the contour" and left-sided, when a circle of radius between 2 and 3 puts that pole inside C and makes the term right-sided.
fix: A pole at z = 2 in an annulus that excludes it, say 1 < |z| < 2: the contour has radius less than 2, so the pole lies outside C. The term is left-sided: −2ⁿu[−n−1].

problem: Garbled expression: "For n n−1 = zn/(z − 0.5) has a negative power of z". The condition on n and the expression for X(z) zⁿ⁻¹ are both unreadable.
fix: For n < 0, X(z) zⁿ⁻¹ = zⁿ/(z − 0.5) has a negative power of z, so z = 0 is a pole of order |n|. If it lies inside C its residue adds to x[n].

problem: The complex-pole pair is written rncos(ωn) and rnsin(ωn), which reads as r·n·cos(ωn).
fix: Combine conjugate poles into a quadratic factor and use the pairs rⁿcos(ωn) and rⁿsin(ωn).

problem: Exponents are left as plain characters: "X(z) = Σ x[n] z−n" and "coefficient of z−n" read as z minus n.
fix: X(z) = Σ x[n] z⁻ⁿ, and read x[n] as the coefficient of z⁻ⁿ.

problem: The bullet uses "pknu[n]" while the table writes aⁿu[n]; the missing superscript makes the two look like different results.
fix: Use pkⁿu[n] in the bullet so it matches the table entry aⁿu[n] with a = pk.
